speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) what is the number of workers who have lodged a complaint against their employers for failing to provide itemised payslips since the time such payslips were made mandatory on 1 April 2016; (b) how many companies have failed to issue itemised payslips to their workers; and (c) what measures are being taken to educate and help employers, especially those in small-to-medium enterprises, in complying with the legislation to issue itemised payslips to their employees.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Employers were given sufficient time to prepare with ample access to solutions and resources to comply.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: When the requirement was introduced, MOM worked with the tripartite partners and industry associations, such as the National Trades Union Congress (NTUC) U Care Centre, U SME, Federation of Merchants’ Associations Singapore, and the Association of Small and Medium Enterprises, to increase awareness and offer solutions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: In fact, these templates can be downloaded from the MOM website in four vernacular languages.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Small and medium enterprises (SMEs) can also tap on the Human Resource (HR) Shared Services providers, such as those appointed under Enterprise Singapore’s HR Shared Services scheme, to help them to be in full compliance with the law.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: First, what were some of the main reasons cited by the employers for not issuing the payslips?

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Second, would MOM expect these errant employers to issue backdated payslips to their workers to ensure they were properly remunerated?

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Third, does MOM know what proportion of employers have adopted the issuance of itemised payslips today?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: MOM has continued to educate by putting in more effort into education to help employers, especially our SMEs, to comply with the requirement.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We have also worked with the likes of the Singapore National Employers Federation, Singapore Business Federation, Association of Small and Medium Enterprises, Tripartite Alliance for Fair and Progressive Employment Practices (TAFEP) and others, to include seminars and workshops to educate them on the requirement and provide, as I have mentioned earlier, blank basic templates that they can use and download quite easily.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: In addition, Enterprise Singapore has also appointed a pool of service providers that can help provide outsourcing of data processing and HR-related administration, and the aim is to help SMEs comply with the law as well.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But MOM does get into details in the event of a dispute, in terms of asking the employer to provide various information, such as past payments, as well as other information, such as timesheets, long medical leave and other benefits that the employee may require.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, we do not make them print out and backdate the payslips.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But in the event that they are required, the employee can ask the employer or come to MOM or the Tripartite Alliance for Dispute Management for mediation, if need be.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But we also recognise that there is some non-compliance, that last 5%.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, these establishments will be required to attend corrective clinics which will be conducted by TAFEP and the tripartite partners.
